LanguageData.MDT_VerTitle: mod may not support your game version
LanguageData.MDT_VerExplain: {0} lists support for {1}, but you are on RimWorld {2}. Version mismatches are a common source of errors.
LanguageData.MDT_VerFix: Update the mod, or look for a continued or updated version. If it plays fine, you can ignore this.

LanguageData.MDT_ReplaceFix: Switch to {0}. The link above opens it on the Workshop.
LanguageData.MDT_IncompatExplain: {0} is known to be incompatible with {1}, and both are active. This can cause errors.
LanguageData.MDT_IncompatFix: Remove one of the two mods, or check their pages for a compatibility patch.
LanguageData.MDT_AboutIncompatExplain: {0} is marked as incompatible with {1} in a mod's own About.xml, and both are active. Incompatible mods are a common cause of errors like this.
LanguageData.MDT_CommUpdateTip: Download the latest community databases (updated-mod replacements and known incompatibilities). Opt-in, runs in the background, cached for offline use.

LanguageData.MDT_HarmonyConflictExplain: The method {0} in this error is changed by {2} mods using Harmony: {1}. When two mods change the same method, one can break the other, and this often produces errors whose stack trace looks like vanilla code.
LanguageData.MDT_HarmonyConflictFix: Disable these mods one at a time to find the pair that conflicts, then report it to both authors with this stack trace. A patch load-order or compatibility mod may also resolve it.
LanguageData.MDT_HarmonyPatchedTitle: a mod changed the method in this error
LanguageData.MDT_HarmonyPatchedExplain: The method {0} in this error is changed by {1} using Harmony. The error can come from that change even though the stack trace shows the original vanilla code.
LanguageData.MDT_HarmonyPatchedFix: If the error repeats, disable that mod to confirm it is the cause, then report it to the author with this stack trace.
LanguageData.MDT_DepMissingTitle: a required mod is missing or inactive
LanguageData.MDT_DepMissingExplain: {0} requires {1}, which is not active. Missing required mods are the most common cause of errors like missing defs, missing types and unresolved references.
LanguageData.MDT_DepMissingFix: Install or activate the required mod, then restart. A mod-list sorter can also add and place it for you.
LanguageData.MDT_DepOrderTitle: a mod is in the wrong load order
LanguageData.MDT_DepOrderExplain: {0} is loaded in the wrong order:
LanguageData.MDT_DepOrderFix: Move it as noted above, or press Sort in the mod list to fix load order automatically.
LanguageData.MDT_DepSummaryTitle: missing required mods can cause this
LanguageData.MDT_DepSummaryExplain: {0} active mods are missing a required mod, the usual root cause of missing def, missing type and unresolved reference errors:
LanguageData.MDT_DepSummaryFix: Install or activate the mods listed above, then restart. A mod-list sorter can add and order dependencies for you.
LanguageData.MDT_GlHarmonyDef: A shared library that lets mods change the game's built-in code at runtime. Most code mods use it. When two mods change the same thing, they can clash.
LanguageData.MDT_GlTranspilerDef: The most invasive kind of Harmony patch: it rewrites a method's instructions directly. Powerful, but the most likely to break when the game or another mod updates.
LanguageData.MDT_GlCrossRefDef: One piece of game data pointing at another by name. An unresolved cross-reference means the thing it points at was not found, usually a missing or wrongly ordered mod.
LanguageData.MDT_GlDefDef: A piece of game data defined in a mod's XML: an item, building, recipe, animal, and so on. Its defName is its unique id.
LanguageData.MDT_GlXpathDef: The addressing language a mod's patch uses to find the exact game data it wants to change. A failed patch usually means its XPath no longer matches anything.
LanguageData.MDT_GlPatchOpDef: A rule in a mod that edits another mod's or the game's XML data at load time. It fails quietly when its target has moved or another mod changed it first.
LanguageData.MDT_GlStackTraceDef: The list of methods the game was running when the error happened, newest first. It is the main clue for finding which mod's code is involved.
LanguageData.MDT_GlNullRefDef: Code tried to use something that did not exist. The most common error, usually a mod meeting a situation its author did not expect.
LanguageData.MDT_GlTpsDef: Ticks per second: how fast the simulation runs. An error that fires every tick drags TPS down and makes the game feel slow even at high FPS.
LanguageData.MDT_GlFpsDef: Frames per second: how smoothly the screen draws. An error in drawing code fires every frame and can tank FPS.
LanguageData.MDT_GlLoadOrderDef: The order mods load in. A mod that must load after the mods it depends on will error if it loads too early. A sorter fixes most of these.
LanguageData.MDT_GlPackageIdDef: A mod's unique id, like author.modname. The game uses it to match dependencies and load order, not the display name.
LanguageData.MDT_GlHugsLibDef: A common library mod that many others depend on. If it is missing or outdated, every mod that needs it can fail.
LanguageData.MDT_GlTypeLoadDef: A mod's code could not be loaded, so all of its features and data are disabled. Usually a missing dependency or a version mismatch, often with Harmony.
LanguageData.MDT_GlCompDef: A reusable piece of behavior a mod attaches to a thing (an item, building, or pawn) to give it extra abilities. A buggy comp is a common source of repeating per-tick errors.
LanguageData.MDT_GlHediffDef: Short for health diff: anything on a pawn's health tab, such as a wound, disease, implant, or drug effect. A broken hediff can error every time the pawn updates.
LanguageData.MDT_GlTickDef: The smallest step of the simulation; the game runs 60 per second at normal speed. An error that fires every tick repeats very fast and slows the game.
LanguageData.MDT_GlScribeDef: RimWorld's save and load system. Errors mentioning Scribe happen while writing or reading your save, often because a mod changed since the save was made.
LanguageData.MDT_GlLoadIdDef: The unique id a save uses to link one saved object to another. An unresolved loadID means the linked object is missing from the save, usually from a removed or changed mod.
LanguageData.MDT_GlDefOfDef: A code shortcut a mod uses to grab a specific def by name. Using one before defs finish loading returns nothing, a common startup-timing bug.
LanguageData.MDT_GlGizmoDef: One of the command buttons at the bottom-left when you select something (draft, set area, toggle power). A mod's gizmo code can throw while the button draws.
LanguageData.MDT_GlITabDef: One of the tabs on the panel that opens when you select a thing (Health, Gear, Needs). A broken tab errors when you open it.
LanguageData.MDT_GlMoteDef: A small, short-lived visual effect such as text popups, puffs of smoke, or hearts. Harmless on their own; mote errors are usually cosmetic.
LanguageData.MDT_GlAssemblyDef: A mod's compiled code, shipped as a .dll file. If an assembly fails to load, every feature and def from that mod is disabled at once.
LanguageData.MDT_GlPrePostfixDef: The two gentler kinds of Harmony patch: a prefix runs before the original code, a postfix after. They coexist better than transpilers when several mods patch the same thing - but a prefix can also skip the original method entirely, which silently starves other mods' patches and is a common source of conflicts.
LanguageData.MDT_GlDlcDef: An official paid expansion (Royalty, Ideology, Biotech, Anomaly). A mod that needs one will error if that DLC is not installed and active.
LanguageData.MDT_HardeningDesc: If a window keeps erroring (a black or frozen window), catch it so it cannot freeze the rest of the interface, then close it after a few seconds. Experimental: it changes vanilla behavior and is off by default.
LanguageData.MDT_MapHardening: Experimental: recover broken world and map UI
LanguageData.MDT_MapHardeningDesc: If the world map or in-map UI throws, often a mod hitting a missing faction or null data after your modlist changed, catch it so the rest of the interface still draws instead of loading into a blank or broken world map. Experimental: it changes vanilla behavior and is off by default.
LanguageData.MDT_ModsChangedTip: Mods have changed since this save was made, a common cause of save errors. Click for details.
LanguageData.MDT_ModsChangedIntro: These mods were updated, removed, or added since this save was created. Updated and removed mods are the usual cause of errors on an existing save.
LanguageData.MDT_EvidenceUpdated: {0}\n\nThe files in this mod's folder differ from the ones recorded when the save was made: a file was added, removed, renamed, or changed size. Timestamps are not used, so re-downloads and file copies do not trigger this.
LanguageData.MDT_EvidenceRemoved: {0}\n\nThis mod was active when the save was made and is not loaded now.
LanguageData.MDT_EvidenceAdded: {0}\n\nThis mod is loaded now and was not active when the save was made.
LanguageData.MDT_ModsChangedPresenceOnly: This save was made before mod contents were fingerprinted, so only mods that were added or removed can be listed. Updated mods cannot be detected on this save; save once and the next load will have the full picture.
LanguageData.MDT_ModsChangedPending: Still comparing mod contents in the background - the "updated" list may be incomplete.
LanguageData.MDT_ModsChangedUnverified: {0} mod(s) could not be compared (official content, or a folder that could not be fully read). They are not listed either way.
LanguageData.MDT_SettingDetectModChanges: Detect mods changed since a save
LanguageData.MDT_SettingDetectModChangesTip: Records a fingerprint of each mod's files in the save and compares it on load, so you are told which mods actually changed. Costs one background pass over your mod folders per session (file names and sizes only - no file contents are read).
LanguageData.MDT_UpdateNotesTitle: What's new in Modern Dev Tools
LanguageData.MDT_UpdateNotesBody:
Welcome to Modern Dev Tools, a modern overhaul of RimWorld's developer tools.

New in 1.3 - playing well with others
- Other log mods keep working: HugsLib and Archotech Logs add their own buttons to RimWorld's original debug log. Because this mod replaces that window, those buttons used to disappear silently. They now appear in an add-on tray along the bottom of the modern log - including HugsLib's Share logs, Files and Copy - restyled to match the rest of the window.
- Archotech Logs integration: its Diagnostics and Export windows open straight from the tray, and they follow whichever message you select.
- A Vanilla log button opens RimWorld's original window any time, and a new Log window setting hands the log back to vanilla completely if you would rather another mod own it.

Log spam throttle (optional, off by default)
- When the same error repeats endlessly, RimWorld still builds a full stack trace and writes to the log file for every single repeat. Worse, it only collapses repeats that arrive back to back, so two errors alternating are never collapsed at all.
- Turn this on to stop writing a line after the first few. The first few always come through, the number held back is shown next to the message, and it is counted toward the error's severity - so nothing is hidden from you.
- This hides symptoms, not causes. Fix the underlying error.

Faster panels
- Text measurement, error analysis and mod ranking are now cached instead of being recomputed several times per frame.
- The knowledge base only draws the rows you can actually see, so long lists no longer cost anything off screen.
- The two experimental hardening features and the spam throttle only install their patches while switched on, instead of always running.

Accuracy fixes
- The "mods changed since this save" warning could call a mod updated when it had not been. It compared the mod folder's last-write time, which changes whenever Steam re-downloads identical files, whenever a folder is copied or restored, and whenever anything writes next to the mod - and which does NOT change when a file deep inside is edited. It now compares a fingerprint of the actual files in each mod, with no timestamps involved, and stays silent about any mod it cannot fully verify rather than guessing. The mod's name is also recorded when the save is written, so the list can no longer show the name of a different copy of the same mod.
- A known-issues file shipped by one mod can no longer claim another mod's error. It now applies only to errors that implicate the mod that shipped it, or to the mods and namespaces it names explicitly.
- Removed one knowledge-base entry and three internal match strings that could never match real game output, and corrected the detection of the most common missing-def error.

For mod authors
- Public API v2: add your own knowledge sources, add a button to the log window, or listen for completed analyses. The button signature matches HugsLib's, so one method works with both.
- New: bridge another mod's diagnostics into the log entirely from XML, with no code and no hard dependency.
- See Documentation/RootCauseAnalysis.md.
LanguageData.MDT_DevPaletteEmpty: Pin actions from the dev tools window to add them here.
LanguageData.MDT_NoIgnored: No warnings are being ignored. Open a warning and press Ignore to mute a harmless class of warnings.
LanguageData.MDT_ExtendHint: Add your own analysis: ship a ModernDevTools.ErrorModuleDef or a ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef in XML, or call ModernDevToolsAPI.RegisterModule in C# with your own ErrorModule subclass. Full guide: Documentation/RootCauseAnalysis.md.
LanguageData.MDT_KbButtonTip: Browse everything Modern Dev Tools knows: the issue libraries, community databases, your mods' compatibility and dependencies, live Harmony patches, and the glossary - each with its source.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourcesIntro: Everything Modern Dev Tools shows you is gathered from the sources below. Select one to browse its entries.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourceKnownDesc: Curated, plain-language explanations of common engine and mod errors.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourceBenignDesc: Normal RimWorld log lines recognized as no-fault, so they are never blamed on a mod.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourceCommunityDesc: Opt-in online database of known bugs and fixes, plus issues shipped inside your mods.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourceCompatDesc: Declared and community-known incompatibilities and updated replacements for your mods.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourceDepsDesc: Missing required mods and load-order problems in your active mod list.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourceHarmonyDesc: Live list of game methods that mods change at runtime, and where several collide.
LanguageData.MDT_KbSourceGlossaryDesc: Plain-language definitions of the jargon that shows up in errors.

LanguageData.MDT_KbNoCommunityBugs: No community bug entries are loaded yet. Press Enable and update, or Update info, to download them.
LanguageData.MDT_KbNoShipped: None of your active mods ship their own known-issue file.

LanguageData.MDT_VanillaLogTip: Open RimWorld's original debug log window.\n\n{0} add their own buttons there, and those buttons only appear on the original window.
LanguageData.MDT_CompatHint: {0} also add buttons to RimWorld's original debug log. Those buttons only appear on the original window - open it any time with the "Vanilla log" button.
LanguageData.MDT_CompatHugsLibDetail: Share logs, Files and Copy buttons, plus any log buttons other mods add through HugsLib.
LanguageData.MDT_CompatArchotechDetail: Diagnostics, Export and log colouring buttons.
LanguageData.MDT_YieldLogWindowDesc: Hand the debug log back to RimWorld. The hotkey, the dev toolbar button and auto-open all open the original window again, so mods that add buttons to it work exactly as they would without this mod. The modern log stays reachable from the dev tools window.
LanguageData.MDT_LogDecorators: Detected on the vanilla log window: {0}
LanguageData.MDT_ThrottleDesc: When the same log line repeats over and over, stop writing it after the first few. RimWorld builds a full stack trace and writes to the log file for every repeat, even ones it then discards, so a runaway error costs speed on top of whatever is already wrong. The first few always come through, and the number held back is shown next to the message. This hides symptoms, not causes.
LanguageData.MDT_ThrottleSummary: held back {0} repeats of a log line after the first {1}. Fix the underlying error to stop it.
LanguageData.MDT_SuppressedTip: {0} further repeats were held back by the log spam throttle.
